question: A 29-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 0 at 11 weeks' gestation comes to the physician because of a 2-day history of left lower extremity pain and swelling. Her temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F). Physical examination shows a tender, palpable cord on the lateral aspect of the left lower leg. The overlying skin is erythematous and indurated. Duplex ultrasound shows vascular wall thickening and subcutaneous edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "29-year-old woman, gravida 1, para 0 at 11 weeks' gestation" -> "left lower extremity pain and swelling" -> "tender, palpable cord on the lateral aspect of the left lower leg" -> "erythematous and indurated skin overlying the cord" -> "Duplex ultrasound shows vascular wall thickening and subcutaneous edema" -> "Deep vein thrombosis" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 29-year-old pregnant woman with left lower extremity pain, swelling, tender cord, erythematous skin, and vascular wall thickening on ultrasound is deep vein thrombosis. This is supported by the presence of a tender, palpable cord on the lateral aspect of the leg, erythematous and indurated skin, and findings of vascular wall thickening and subcutaneous edema on Duplex ultrasound. The evidence path linking ultrasonography, Doppler, and Duplex to deep vein thrombosis further supports this diagnosis.
analysis: The core medical principle in this case is the presentation of a pregnant woman with left lower extremity pain, swelling, a tender cord, erythematous skin, and vascular wall thickening on ultrasound. These findings are highly suggestive of deep vein thrombosis, especially given the presence of a palpable cord, erythema, and edema. The enhanced information further supports this diagnosis based on the specific ultrasound findings and clinical features.
